findings.finding: AC-3's invariant conflates two distinct countable events in the LLM structured-retry protocol: 'outer Agent run' (Agent object construction) versus `agent.run_sync` calls. On the prompted output-repair path a single constructed Agent issues `output_retries+1` `agent.run_sync` calls in a loop (structured_run.py:161-163), whereas the 895c downgrade constructs a SECOND Agent (structured_run.py:128 native, then 157 prompted). The test as described ('one `agent.run_sync` on the happy path and exactly two ... never a third') counts run_sync, but when structured_retry_limit>0 and the first prompted reply is malformed-then-valid, run_sync fires more than once on ONE Agent — which the 'never a third' bound would falsely trip unless the test scopes the count to Agent constructions (or to the well-formed-first-response case only).
scenarios: A prompted-path structured call with structured_retry_limit>=1 whose first reply fails parse but second succeeds — fires two agent.run_sync on one Agent, no downgrade
The 895c downgrade case where each of native and prompted paths could each issue repair run_syncs
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC-3 to assert 'exactly one Agent construction on the happy path; exactly two Agent constructions (native then prompted) only on the 895c downgrade', and separately assert 'one agent.run_sync when the first response is well-formed'. Have the test count Agent constructions for the downgrade bound and run_sync only under the well-formed-first-response fixture.
